steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: An open-loop control system has no feedback; the output is not checked against the desired value, so errors are not corrected automatically.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A closed-loop (feedback) control system measures the output and compares it with the set point, adjusting the input to reduce any error.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Closed-loop control uses a sensor to measure the output, a comparator to find the error, and a controller to correct it.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A microcontroller is a single-chip computer containing a processor, memory and input/output peripherals for embedded control.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of open-loop control. | Q: Describe the three essential components of a closed-loop control system. | Q: Explain how PWM can be used to control the brightness of an LED.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Advantage: simple and low cost. Disadvantage: cannot correct for disturbances or changes in the system since there is no feedback. | A sensor to measure the output, a comparator to calculate the error between the output and set point, and a controller to adjust the input to reduce the error. | A PWM signal rapidly switches the LED on and off; increasing the duty cycle (on-time proportion) increases the average current and brightness, while decreasing it dims the LED.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always draw a block diagram for control system questions, showing sensor, comparator, controller and actuator with feedback path. Distinguish clearly between open-loop (no feedback) and closed-loop (feedback with error correction). For microcontroller questions, mention the specific peripherals needed: ADC for analogue sensors, PWM for motor/LED control. When describing a control program, outline the loop structure: read inputs → process data → update outputs → repeat. Explain the purpose of each component in a block diagram rather than just naming it.
